s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath with evidence of cardiac and respiratory compromise
salient_findings: Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function
Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli
Elevated troponin and N-terminal pro brain-type natriuretic peptide levels
key_facts: 82-year-old man
History of coronary artery disease with stent placement 10 years ago
History of surgically treated colon cancer
Episodes of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath began one day before admission
Heart rate: 114 beats/min
Blood pressure: 94/62 mm Hg
Oxygen saturation: 91% on 4 L/min of supplemental oxygen
Respiratory rate: 28 breaths per minute
Troponin I level: 0.135 µg/L (peaked at 0.499 µg/L)
D-dimer level: >109.52 nmol/L
N-terminal pro brain-type natriuretic peptide level: 562.21 pmol/L
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function
CT Angiogram showed acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms with evidence of extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli on CT Angiogram

shortlist.label: Acute Cor Pulmonale
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function on transthoracic echocardiogram and evidence of pulmonary hypertension

shortlist.label: Cardiogenic Shock
shortlist.why_kept: Hypotension, tachycardia, and elevated troponin levels suggest cardiac compromise

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Crisis
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of pulmonary hypertension on CT Angiogram and transthoracic echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Right Ventricular Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin levels and dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function on transthoracic echocardiogram

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of dizziness, syncope, and shortness of breath, combined with the CT Angiogram showing acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli, strongly support this diagnosis. The elevated D-dimer level and troponin I level also indicate a pulmonary embolism.

rejected.label: Acute Cor Pulmonale
rejected.why: While the patient has a dilated right ventricle with reduced systolic function, this is more likely a consequence of the pulmonary embolism rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cardiogenic Shock
rejected.why: The patient's blood pressure is low, but the primary issue appears to be the pulmonary embolism rather than a cardiogenic cause.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Hypertension Crisis
rejected.why: The patient does have pulmonary hypertension, but this is likely secondary to the pulmonary embolism rather than a primary crisis.

rejected.label: Right Ventricular Infarction
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin I levels, the primary diagnosis of pulmonary embolism better explains the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.

gold: Pulmonary Reperfusion Injury after catheter-directed thrombectomy for acute pulmonary embolism
